reading_plan: Source title: House Bill 1193 (As Passed House and Senate): Georgia Early Literacy Act of 2026. Source type: government_policy. This is the Georgia General Assembly’s 42-page HB 1193/AP, labeled AS PASSED HOUSE AND SENATE, not a signed enactment in the supplied text. A long title precedes four parts: coaching and credentials; revisions to the Early Literacy and Dyslexia Act, materials, and governance; attendance, readiness, and promotion; and effectiveness/conflicts. It is dense, line-numbered amendatory legislation with nested Code subsections, underlined additions, and struck-through deletions. I first survey the complete structure, then follow the printed order at subsection scale, usually less than a page per step, splitting long lists and procedures. I compare the extracted text with all supplied page images to recover the language after amendment, distinguish mandates from permissions and encouragement, preserve dates and conditions, and mark repetition without counting the same provision again. Cross-references are recorded as printed without supplying outside legal content or evaluating the policy.

reading_path.moves: Identifies HB 1193/AP as AS PASSED HOUSE AND SENATE, names its sponsors, and announces amendments to Title 20. The long title previews coaching, materials, screening, governance, attendance, and placement; those operative provisions are recorded where they occur below.
reading_path.meaning: The opening frames literacy as a statewide education effort spanning classroom support, state administration, and early grade progression. This is a passed bill text; the document does not itself establish a date of gubernatorial approval.

reading_path.moves: Supplies a short title.

claims.text: This Act shall be known and may be cited as the "Georgia Early Literacy Act of 2026."

reading_path.meaning: The named Act now moves from its broad title to the personnel and resources intended to carry out literacy work.

reading_path.moves: Changes existing law by adding a definition and an appropriation-dependent reimbursement grant.

claims.text: As used in this paragraph, the term 'eligible school' means a school with any of grades kindergarten through three.

Subject to General Assembly appropriations, the State Board of Education shall provide grants to local units of administration with eligible schools to reimburse expenditures sufficient for the beginning salary and benefits of one school based literacy coach per eligible school.
An eligible school with 200 or fewer full-time equivalent students shall earn 50 percent of that amount.

reading_path.meaning: The bill begins with a funding mechanism, with both an appropriation condition and a smaller allocation for small schools; it does not state an unconditional funded coach entitlement.

reading_path.moves: Assigns standard-setting authority and sets an open list of minimum coach qualifications.

claims.text: The State Board of Education, in collaboration with the Office of Student Achievement, shall establish minimum qualifications and duties for school based literacy coaches.
Minimum qualifications shall include, but shall not be limited to, certification by the Professional Standards Commission.
School based literacy coaches must have at least five years of documented successful classroom teaching or literacy intervention experience at assigned grade levels.

School based literacy coaches must know scientifically based reading research and have special expertise in quality reading instruction and intervention, dyslexia specific interventions, and data analysis.

reading_path.meaning: Funding is followed by a professional specification: the bill sets a floor while allowing further qualifications.

reading_path.moves: Prescribes the first four duties in an expressly nonexhaustive list, including a numerical classroom-time minimum.

claims.text: School based literacy coaches shall coach educators using nonevaluative, evidence based practices, including modeling instruction, analyzing instructional practice and data, actionable feedback, and side-by-side classroom support.
They shall collaborate with the principal to create a strategic literacy coaching plan.
They shall spend no less than 70 percent of the school day in classrooms working directly with students and teachers.
They shall prioritize teachers, activities, and roles with the greatest impact on student reading achievement, such as classroom coaching and mentoring.

reading_path.meaning: The role is organized around classroom practice and a protected share of classroom time, rather than simply possession of a credential.

reading_path.moves: Continues the open minimum-duty list with data use, implementation fidelity, and practice assessment.

claims.text: Coaches shall analyze screening, diagnostic, and progress monitoring data to inform instruction, grouping, and intervention within a multi-tiered system of supports framework.
They shall synthesize student performance and educator practice data to set coaching goals and design targeted, needs based educator support.
They shall support implementation and monitoring of evidence based literacy curricula and instructional materials with fidelity and alignment to the science of reading.

They shall demonstrate competency through approved, periodic, practice based assessment verifying application of the science of reading, learning science, and instructional science to explicit, systematic, evidence based literacy instruction directly with students.

reading_path.meaning: The bill connects coaching to student evidence and curriculum implementation, and subjects the coach’s own practical competence to recurring verification.

reading_path.moves: Prohibits incompatible assignments, sets an implementation deadline, and preserves alternative funding.

claims.text: A school based literacy coach shall not be authorized or required to perform administrative functions or duties, including, but not limited to, rotating duty assignments or service as evaluator, substitute teacher, assessment coordinator, or school administrator.
A school based literacy coach shall not be invited, required, or permitted to attend placement committee meetings.
A school based literacy coach shall not be designated as a teacher of record.
By August 1, 2026, the State Board shall establish implementation policies, rules, and regulations, including, but not limited to, the grant request and receipt process.
Nothing in the Code section shall be construed to prohibit local units of administration from hiring or contracting with school based literacy coaches using other funds available for such purpose.

reading_path.meaning: The boundaries reinforce the classroom coaching role. The final saving clause allows local hiring outside this grant mechanism.

reading_path.moves: Changes existing law by creating a RESA employment, assignment, reporting, and cooperation structure.

claims.text: Each regional educational service agency (RESA) board of control shall authorize regional literacy coaches and regional leadership literacy coaches to provide coaching, support, and related services to local systems and other public schools in its service area.

Each RESA board shall assign regional literacy coaches in collaboration with the State Literacy Director and Georgia Literacy Coach Coordinator; at least one regional leadership literacy coach shall be the primary contact with system and school leaders.
Authorized regional literacy and regional leadership literacy coaches shall be employed by the RESA and report to its director.
Both kinds of regional coach and the RESA director shall cooperate fully with the Georgia Literacy Coordinating Committee, State Literacy Director, and Georgia Literacy Coach Coordinator.
Both kinds of regional coach shall cooperate fully with observation, evaluation, and feedback from the Georgia Literacy Coach Coordinator or designee.

reading_path.meaning: The school role acquires a regional support structure with RESA employment and statewide coordination running alongside the local reporting line.

reading_path.moves: Sets regional coach standards in open minimum lists. Certification, five years of successful teaching/intervention, reading and dyslexia expertise, nonevaluative coaching practices, and student-data analysis repeat the school coach standards already recorded, now expressly applied to regional coaches.

claims.text: The State Board, collaborating with the Office of Student Achievement, shall establish minimum qualifications and duties for regional literacy coaches; the enumerated qualifications and duties are not exhaustive.
Regional literacy coaches shall collaborate with school principals, school based literacy coaches, and Department of Education and Office of Student Achievement representatives.
Regional literacy coaches shall provide ongoing support for effective implementation and continuous improvement of comprehensive literacy programs in local systems and public schools.

Regional literacy coaches shall provide ongoing professional learning activities and materials for teachers and literacy coaches, including science of reading research and curriculum based professional learning to support application in instruction.

reading_path.meaning: The repeated professional floor ties regional and school coaches together, while the new duties emphasize sustained support across schools.

reading_path.moves: Creates a distinct leadership coach qualification framework, again expressly nonexhaustive; certification and reading/dyslexia/data expertise repeat the earlier professional floor.

claims.text: The State Board and Office of Student Achievement shall establish minimum qualifications and duties for regional leadership literacy coaches.
Their qualifications shall include at least five years of documented success as a literacy coach or K-3 classroom teacher or administrator.
They shall have successful experience leading a school, district, or regional literacy program, to include principal, curriculum director, superintendent, or state-level literacy specialist roles.
They shall have extensive knowledge of implementing a structured literacy program founded in the science of reading.
They shall have successful experience working with adult learners.
They shall have exceptional interpersonal skills.
They shall have exceptional communication skills.
They shall have successful experience leading educational programs and/or initiatives.

reading_path.meaning: Leadership coaching adds organizational and adult-learning experience to the instructional expertise required throughout the coaching structure.

reading_path.moves: Prescribes the first part of an open list of regional leadership duties.

claims.text: Regional leadership literacy coaches shall participate in literacy improvement and coaching professional learning within the RESA network.
They shall collaborate with superintendents and principals to create literacy rich environments, prioritizing schools that include K-3.
They shall join superintendents and principals in side-by-side classroom observations supporting teachers and paraprofessionals in applying the science of reading.
They shall help regional coaches prioritize local system needs based on student data and communication with system leaders.
They shall facilitate communication and collaboration between systems and regional coaches.

reading_path.meaning: The leadership role brings school and district leaders into classroom observation and uses their communication with coaches to organize support.

reading_path.moves: Completes the leadership duties with planning and community and postsecondary relationships.

claims.text: Leadership coaches shall guide systems in developing and implementing local unified literacy plans.
They shall facilitate system-community collaboration supporting literacy from birth to age five.
They shall facilitate collaboration with local and regional postsecondary institutions.
They shall collaborate with other regional leadership literacy coaches.

reading_path.meaning: The remit extends beyond currently enrolled K-3 students to early childhood, institutional partnerships, and local planning.

reading_path.moves: Changes existing law by requiring an endorsement and specifying its training content and deadline.

claims.text: No later than December 31, 2026, the Professional Standards Commission shall establish a literacy coaching endorsement for teachers and other certificated personnel trained in an evidence based approach to oral and written language aligned to the science of reading and founded on how children learn to read.
That approach is characterized by explicit, systematic, cumulative, diagnostic instruction in phonology, sound-symbol association, syllable instruction, morphology, syntax, and semantics.

Endorsement requirements shall include training in universal reading screeners for measuring and monitoring foundational literacy progress, guidance to parents, and training or guidance to teachers and other school personnel.

reading_path.meaning: Part I closes by adding a formal training credential alongside the job qualifications, classroom duties, and regional organization.

reading_path.location: Part II, Section 2-1; amendment instruction and 20-2-153.1(a.1), p. 9
reading_path.moves: Changes existing law: repeals and reserves (b)(2), replaces (b)(6), renumbers former (b)(16) as (17), adds a new (b)(16), and revises/adds the stated subsections. Adds legislative intent rather than empirical findings.

claims.text: The General Assembly intends early literacy instruction to be comprehensive, focused on structured literacy and foundational literacy skills, aligned to the science of reading, and anchored by high-quality instructional materials aligned to that science.
The stated intent is that educators shall be given access to science of reading research and receive comprehensive curriculum based professional learning supporting its instructional application.
The stated intent is that continuing parental and guardian involvement in comprehensive statewide literacy efforts shall be encouraged and integrated into children’s education.

reading_path.meaning: The text now expressly names the instructional orientation already embedded in the coaching provisions, while presenting family participation as part of the same effort.

reading_path.moves: Replaces the dyslexia definition and adds a unified literacy plan definition and required components.

claims.text: 'Dyslexia' shall have the same meaning as the definition adopted and amended from time to time by the International Dyslexia Association and approved by the board and posted on the websites of the department and the Office of Student Achievement.

support.text: The definition incorporates the International Dyslexia Association definition as amended from time to time, subject to board approval and website posting; the bill does not print that external definition.

claims.text: 'Unified literacy plan' means a comprehensive, evidence based framework to ensure coherent, aligned, and continuous literacy development for learners from birth through career readiness.

As appropriate to grades served, the plan shall establish measurable goals for all tested grades, using statewide assessments and approved screener data to monitor progress, guide instructional decisions, and evaluate program effectiveness.
As appropriate to grades served, it shall include explicit collaboration strategies with birth-to-five early learning providers supporting school readiness and early language development.
As appropriate to grades served, it shall establish literacy transition plans for the transition from kindergarten to elementary school.

reading_path.meaning: The framework spans birth through career readiness but conditions its concrete requirements on the grades an institution serves. Dyslexia is defined through an external organization rather than reproduced here.

reading_path.moves: Retains literacy metric rulemaking and amends the materials deadline, recommendation process, and alignment standard; deletions and additions are resolved from the page image.

claims.text: The board, consulting the department and Office of Student Achievement, shall establish necessary policies, rules, and regulations for uniform grade-appropriate literacy metrics.

By March 1, 2027, the board shall, upon the Office of Student Achievement’s recommendation, approve high-quality instructional materials aligned to the science of reading for teaching K-3 students to read.

By that same date it shall establish a procedure for each public school and local system to certify annually to the department that locally approved materials and content constitute high-quality materials aligned to the science of reading.

reading_path.meaning: The intent is translated into state metrics, approval, and recurring local certification. The printed deadline here is March 1, before the task force materials deadline encountered later.

reading_path.moves: Replaces the old screener submission/review and approval language, deletes former criteria, and inserts a new list and capabilities. Deleted center reviews and old dates are not operative provisions.

claims.text: By April 1, 2028, and April 1 every third year thereafter, the board shall approve, upon recommendation of the Office of Student Achievement, a list of at least two and at most five universal reading screeners for public school and system comprehensive literacy programs, one free of charge.
Each approved screener shall provide screening and diagnostic capabilities for progress monitoring.

Each shall measure, at a minimum, foundational reading skills, including, but not limited to, phonological awareness, oral language, alphabetic principle (including letter naming, letter sound, and sound letter correspondences), decoding, encoding, accuracy, vocabulary, and comprehension.
Each shall identify students significantly at risk of not attaining grade level reading proficiency, including, but not limited to, students with dyslexia characteristics.

Each shall have robust reporting capabilities, including direct provision to the department and Office of Student Achievement of results by student; student subgroups by grade, educational program, demographics, and other task-force criteria; school; and system.

reading_path.meaning: The screener rules now combine a bounded choice of products with broad minimum measurement and reporting capabilities.

Programs shall promote teachers’ ability to teach all students, including those with dyslexia, and ensure teachers and coaches can use approved screeners and assessment data to tailor instruction.

One program shall be statewide, comprehensive, curriculum based structured literacy professional learning aligned to and including science of reading research for K-3 teachers and coaches; it shall be recommended by the Georgia Literacy Task Force.

claims.text: Using school based coaches and other available resources, each public school and local system shall provide K-3 teacher support that shall include onsite professional learning and research materials in science of reading, structured literacy, foundational literacy, and evidence based decision making.
Support shall include demonstrated lessons applying that learning and research in instruction.
Support shall include school based coaches working side-by-side with teachers in classrooms.
Support shall include school based coaches working directly with individual students and small groups as time permits.
Support shall include prompt feedback to improve instruction.

claims.text: The Professional Standards Commission shall adopt core-curriculum rules for every state approved educator preparation program; the following criteria are minimum inclusions, not an exhaustive list.
Criteria shall require board content standards aligned to the science of reading to guide curricula and instruction.
Evidence based reading teaching standards shall be exclusively aligned to the science of reading.
Those standards shall prepare teachers for explicit, systematic, sequential, diagnostic, cumulative instruction in phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, and text comprehension.
Those standards shall employ multisensory and multimodal intervention strategies.
Criteria shall include content based literacy and mathematics practices.
Criteria shall include appropriate strategies for English language learners.
Criteria shall include appropriate strategies for students with disabilities.
Criteria shall include strategies, including but not limited to assessment results, to identify strengths and weaknesses and differentiate instruction by student need.
Criteria shall include strategies and practices supporting research based content aligned to state standards and grading practices.
Criteria shall include early identification of reading deficiency.
Criteria shall include strategies supporting educational technology and distance learning.
